findings.summary: The export expands every lot/order into one row per conversion document without enforcing EXCEL_MAX_ROWS. The supplied exact projection is 1,807,231 rows, exceeding Excel's 1,048,576-row worksheet limit, so the required ordinary single-sheet workbook cannot remain valid/downloadable.

The implementation materializes the entire expanded dataset with nested flatMap calls before writing it, with no bounded or streaming path and no capacity error. This can cause excessive browser memory use or failure before workbook generation.

unverified: No tests are shown for the default annual dataset, worksheet row limits, browser memory behavior, workbook generation/download success, or boundary cases at and above 1,048,576 rows.
The behavior of writeSingleBrowserWorksheet when given more than Excel's worksheet capacity is not provided, including whether it rejects, truncates, or emits an invalid artifact.
The reconciliation behavior is unverified: no evidence shows that exported row counts and source records are checked for omission, duplication, or truncation.

findings.summary: displayedClosing subtracts only expense and fx_eur consumption, omitting the supported fx_other category. The observed 1,494,440 TRY fx_other total therefore causes the displayed closing balance to be overstated by exactly 1,494,440 TRY and prevents reconciliation.
The new API returns only a calculated closing value; it does not display the required exact opening, inflow, outflow, conversion, and closing turnover for every pool consumer category.

unverified: No tests are shown, so exact reconciliation across all supported consumption types, numeric precision behavior, and handling of unknown or malformed consumption types cannot be verified.
The supplied diff does not define Pool or sum, so type correctness, amount-field aggregation, and empty-input behavior cannot be verified.

findings.summary: Each detail amount is rounded independently, so the returned amounts are not guaranteed to sum to the currency-rounded source amount. This directly violates exact-to-the-cent reconciliation and is consistent with the reported 1578 TRY aggregate drift; allocate residual cents deterministically after initial rounding.

The function neither validates nor normalizes shares, so shares that do not sum exactly to 1 (including empty, negative, non-finite, or malformed values) can produce an allocation total unrelated to the source amount.

Binary floating-point multiplication and Math.round introduce currency edge-case errors (including asymmetric behavior for negative half-cent values); integer minor-unit or decimal arithmetic is needed for reliable cent allocation.

unverified: No tests are shown for exact reconciliation across varying row counts, fractional shares, rounding ties, negative values, zero/empty inputs, or large amounts.
The required behavior for invalid shares and for distributing residual cents among detail rows is unspecified in the supplied material.

findings.summary: The verify script no longer runs `prisma generate`, so schema changes such as `newcrmChangedSince` can be typechecked against stale generated clients, violating the required release-gate ordering.

The `|| echo existing Prisma mismatch` fallback converts every non-zero TypeScript result into success when `echo` succeeds, masking Prisma mismatches and unrelated type errors instead of preserving a non-zero release-gate result.
A temporary local reviewer probe is added to the release tree despite the frozen acceptance criterion excluding reviewer probes.
Private root-cause scratch notes are added to the release tree despite the frozen acceptance criterion excluding private review-run notes.
